assertions.notes: PUT /operator/reservations/setup/locations/v17plv08r5v357bie335lyq8/settings with {holdMinutes:3, expectedVersion:58} -> 200 (version 59); DB row showed hold_minutes=3. Hold H1 (2026-11-15 17:00, party 2, areaPref G9-Area-Strict) -> POST /reservations/holds 201, expiresAt = now+3min, occupancy tbl_00d903ae (G9-2, the only table of the single-table area) 17:00-18:30 active=1. While H1 was live the 17:00 and 17:15 slots were no longer offered in G9-Area-Strict (mapped to G4-Area) — the held unit was withheld. 3.5 min later, after the tick sweep, the H1 row was status=expired with occupancy active=0 and availability showed 17:00 G9-Area-Strict again. A fresh hold H2 -> 201 and POST /reservations with a different guest (+1555555341) -> 201, confirmation 75CKZHEQ (rsv_c5872d07).
assertions.limitations: The public availability endpoint has no area filter, so 'the slot is offered again' was judged by the slot's seating-area mapping returning to G9-Area-Strict (the single-table area whose table H1 held); the location has other tables, so the 17:00 time chip itself never disappeared.

assertions.notes: Expired hold H1's token -> POST /reservations returned 410 {"error":"hold_expired"}; the reservation count for that slot was 1 before and 1 after, and no reservation row is linked to H1's hold id (its row stayed status=expired). The literal second step was executed exactly: after the successful booking (H2 -> 75CKZHEQ) a retry with the same body, a fresh Idempotency-Key and a different phone (+1555555343) returned 410 hold_expired and created no second row (count stayed 1) — the consumed hold token is refused with the documented non-active-hold code. The 409-with-alternatives path was reproduced where the slot is genuinely exhausted: a fresh hold for the now-taken last unit of the single-table area returned 409 {"error":"slot_unavailable"} with 6 same-day alternatives and no second reservation row.
assertions.limitations: Literal deviation: the contract expects the same-body booking retry to answer 409 slot_unavailable; it answers 410 hold_expired (the hold token was consumed by the successful booking). The 409 slot_unavailable + alternatives is produced by a fresh hold attempt for the exhausted unit, which is the only path that can reach that code. If the literal 409-on-retry is binding, this assertion is a partial mismatch rather than a product bug; no double booking occurs either way.

assertions.notes: PUT guestModifyCutoffMin=100000 -> 400 {"error":"invalid", fields:[guestModifyCutoffMin, guest_modify_cutoff_min], issue too_big}. Used the API maximum 10080 (PUT -> 200, version 61) with a booking inside that window: hold + booking on 2026-10-18 19:00 (rsv_9add607f, EG35MGPS) ~1 day out, so the deadline was in the past. GET /reservations/manage -> 200 {status: booked, canModify: false, canCancel: false}, cancelDeadline 2026-10-11T23:00:00.000Z (before now 2026-10-17T14:54Z). POST /reservations/manage/modify -> 409 modify_closed; POST /reservations/manage/cancel -> 409 cancel_closed. The booking was unchanged (status booked, cancelled_by empty, version 1, updated_at identical). guest_modify_cutoff_min restored to 120 and verified (API + DB, final version 66).
assertions.limitations: The contract's literal value 100000 is outside the settings schema (guestModifyCutoffMin max 10_080, packages/reservations/src/schemas/setup.ts), so it cannot be set through the operator settings API; the assertion's observable requirements were reproduced with the maximum accepted value plus a booking inside it. Booking was made on 2026-10-18 (not an owned registry date) because a >7-day-out booking cannot be inside any API-accepted cutoff.

assertions.notes: Step 1 passed: Sites hold at 12:00 on 2026-11-15 in the single-table area (G9-Area-Strict) with the countdown visible; POST /reservations/holds -> 201 (hld_00330bce, G9-2 occupied 12:00-13:30). Step 2 FAILED as specified: GET /operator/reservations/book/availability?locationId=...&date=2026-11-15&partySize=2 returned 200 and still offered the 12:00 slot with available:true (suggestedTableIds [tbl_08a45749]); scoped with areaId=area_9f595e43 (the held area) it also returned available:true and even suggested tbl_00d903ae (G9-2), the exact table the live hold occupies. getOperatorAvailability builds its occupancy set from reservations only (rsv-day-feed-service.ts:1363-1375), so live holds never affect the availability read. Step 3 passed: the guest abandoned the hold (tab left, no confirm/release), the row is status=expired with its occupancy active=0, and the sweep tick reported expire_holds ok (0 further holds). Step 4 passed: the operator endpoint offers 12:00 again (available:true), the public endpoint offers 12:00 in G9-Area-Strict, the Sites chip list shows 12:00 G9-Area-Strict again, and the day feed's holds list is empty. Capacity was protected while the hold was live: a second guest's hold for the same slot+area was refused 409 slot_unavailable with alternatives.
assertions.limitations: Pass criterion 'the slot is withheld while the hold is live ... on both channels' is met for the guest channel but not for the staff availability endpoint named in the contract. Mitigating facts: the staff day feed (GET /operator/reservations/book/day) does list the live hold, and the staff booking write path does respect holds (rsv-booking-service.ts passes engineHolds into assignTables), so the gap is confined to the availability read (it can suggest a table that a guest currently holds). Checkpoint note: the contract's literal query `select status from rsv_holds order by created_at desc limit 1` returned 'converted' because my later VAL-ONLINE-011/048 holds are newer; the abandoned hold hld_00330bce-5e3f-42ce-b0ab-fc631801b7a2 is 'expired' (verified by id) and no active occupancy remains for it.
